jp: 来週[らいしゅう]{の|no-possessive}テスト{は|wa-topic}難[むずか]しい{かな|kana-wonder}。
en: I wonder if next week's test will be hard.
why: Musing to yourself about something you cannot know yet takes かな after the plain form.

jp: 山田[やまだ]さん{は|wa-topic}もう宿題[しゅくだい]{を|o-object}出[だ]した{かな|kana-wonder}。
en: I wonder if Mr. Yamada has already handed in the homework.
why: You cannot see whether he has, so you wonder aloud with かな after the plain past form.

jp: 会議[かいぎ]{は|wa-topic}何時[なんじ]{に|ni-time}終[お]わる{かな|kana-wonder}。
en: I wonder what time the meeting will end.
why: A question word plus かな turns the question inward: you ask yourself, not another person.

jp: 今日[きょう]{は|wa-topic}早[はや]く帰[かえ]れる{かな|kana-wonder}。
en: I wonder if I can go home early today.
why: Uncertainty about your own prospects is voiced to yourself with かな.

jp: この問題[もんだい]{は|wa-topic}どうやって解[と]こう{かな|kana-wonder}。
en: How should I solve this problem, I wonder?
why: Volitional form plus かな with a question word asks yourself how to proceed.

jp: 試験[しけん]{に|ni-target}受[う]かる{かな|kana-wonder}。
en: I wonder if I'll pass the exam.
why: A worry about an uncertain result, spoken to yourself, takes かな.

jp: 先生[せんせい]{に|ni-source}聞[き]い{たら|tara-conditional}、教[おし]えてくれる{かな|kana-wonder}。
en: If I ask the teacher, I wonder if they will explain it to me.
why: You are unsure how the teacher would react, so you wonder aloud with かな.

jp: 新[あたら]しい上司[じょうし]{は|wa-topic}優[やさ]しい人[ひと]{かな|kana-wonder}。
en: I wonder if the new boss is a kind person.
why: かな follows a noun directly when you wonder what someone is like.

jp: 今夜[こんや]{は|wa-topic}図書館[としょかん]{で|de-place}勉強[べんきょう]しよう{かな|kana-wonder}。
en: Maybe I'll study at the library tonight.
why: After the volitional form, かな voices a tentative plan to yourself.

jp: 明日[あした]{の|no-possessive}発表[はっぴょう]{は|wa-topic}うまくいく{かな|kana-wonder}。
en: I wonder if tomorrow's presentation will go well.
why: Nobody can know the outcome yet, so the speaker wonders aloud with かな.

jp: 先生[せんせい]{は|wa-topic}このレポート{を|o-object}もう読[よ]んでくれた{かな|kana-wonder}。
en: I wonder if the teacher has read this report yet.
why: The speaker lacks the information and wonders aloud, so the plain past form takes かな.

jp: 来月[らいげつ]{から|kara-from}、仕事[しごと]{は|wa-topic}忙[いそが]しくなる{かな|kana-wonder}。
en: I wonder if work will get busier from next month.
why: A prediction you are unsure of, said to yourself, ends in かな.
